items: Troubles occuring with the ECT can be caused by either the engine, ECT electrical control or the automatic transmission itself. These three areas should be distinctly isolated before proceeding with troubleshooting.
Troubleshooting should begin with the simplest operation, working up in order of difficulty, but initially determine whether the trouble lies within the engine, electrical control or transmission.
Proceed with the inspection as follows:

content.description: Troubleshooting flowchart showing sequential diagnostic steps from Read Diagnostic Code through Road Test, with associated checks and actions for each step
labels: Electric Control System Check (See page AT-6)

rows: Read the diagnostic code (trouble code) from overdrive indicator light or super monitor display, and perform repairs accordingly.

Check following:
• Fluid level
• Throttle cable mark
• Shift linkage
• Neutral start switch
• Idling rpm ("N" or "P" range 650 rpm)
• Tire inflation pressure
Check engine, torque converter, clutch and brake.

Check Automatic Transmission Assembly
• Check clutch, brake and gear for wear.
Electric Control System Check (See page AT-6)
Check valve body and fluid circuit leakage.

Confirm if trouble lies within ATM.
If noisy or vibrating, cause possibly with either compressor, engine, propeller shaft, tires, etc.
